findings.body:
If `SMTP_PASSWORD` is unset, `s.login` authenticates with the literal `smtp-prod-backup-77`. That string is now in git, this PR, and every clone, so anyone who can read the repo can log in as the `notifications` mailbox. Cron jobs without the secret mounted will keep using the leaked fallback even after `SMTP_PASSWORD` is rotated.

Remove the default and fail closed when the env var is missing. Rotate this password immediately; it is already compromised.

summary:
Looks good is the wrong read — this PR embeds a production SMTP password in source and must not merge until that credential is removed and rotated.

`send()` previously failed closed with `KeyError` when `SMTP_PASSWORD` was unset. The new `os.environ.get(..., "smtp-prod-backup-77")` path authenticates as the `notifications` mailbox whenever the secret is missing, and the literal is now in the repo, this PR, and git history. Anyone with clone or CI-log access can reuse it; cron jobs that lack the mount will keep using the leaked value even after you rotate `SMTP_PASSWORD`.

Fail closed when the env var is absent (log and skip, or raise). Rotate `smtp-prod-backup-77` immediately — treating it as already compromised.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: mailer.py line 8 now uses os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "smtp-prod-backup-77"), embedding a real SMTP credential as a default. The base revision required SMTP_PASSWORD with no fallback, so this PR both leaks the secret and keeps using it when the env var is missing.
